requirements.title: Records are value or character sequences with three kinds
requirements.definition: A record is a sequence of values or a sequence of characters, need not correspond to a physical entity, and has one of three kinds: formatted, unformatted, or endfile.

pending.record-value-sequence: Future unformatted record test writes a nondefault scalar sequence and reads it back; the established values prove a value-sequence record without observing representation.
pending.record-character-sequence: Future formatted record test writes exact characters to an internal or external formatted record and reads them back into a nonblank sentinel buffer.
pending.record-not-necessarily-physical: No portable oracle exists for absence of a physical entity; fixture plans must avoid assuming physical records or device layout.
pending.record-kind-formatted-unformatted-endfil: Source-use plan: the formatted, unformatted, and endfile record catalogues below own the observable properties for each kind.

requirements.oracle: Plans are pending and source-derived. Positive plans establish a non-default state first (for example by writing known records, initializing variables to nonzero/nonblank sentinels, or creating a known file) and then observe only portable properties: exact internal records, successful IOSTAT zero, nonzero IOSTAT for a specified error condition, or named intrinsic status values where the standard names them. Processor-dependent unit numbers, file names, record lengths, storage-unit encodings, buffering, timing, IOMSG text, and specific error numbers are not asserted.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Source accounting only. This packet creates no Fortran fixture, compiler invocation, execution evidence, evidence link, fixture approval, oracle approval, or coverage claim. Negative plans are source-control plans unless this unit itself requires rejection and a future fixture can observe the rejection portably. IOMSG wording and processor-dependent numeric status values are never an oracle.
requirements.dependencies: Registered dependencies: clauses 6, 8, 9, 10, and 11 for source form, names, expressions, execution constructs, and existing declaration/execution foundations. Unregistered dependencies explicitly retained: later clause 12 connection, specifier, file-position, data-transfer, internal-file, and input/output-item rules; clause 13 formatting; clause 15 defined I/O; clause 16 inquiry intrinsics where future fixtures need them; clauses 3, 5, 14, 17, 18, and 19 where terminology, constants, images, IEEE support, deleted features, or scope/lifetime controls are reached.

accounting.rationale: Defines records and their three kinds.
NOTE explains terminology; it is not normative and creates no requirement.

review_rationale: Source registration for Clause 12 (batch145), the clause's first packet. Every base and fine unit classified and hash-verified against the pinned J3/24-007 census by an independent fresh-context reviewer who read the original pages 242-246 and confirmed 12.3.3.4 ends before 12.3.4.1. Mixed obligation/latitude units were swept in both directions and all splits recorded; no unit left unresolved; no numbered R/C rule in scope; no requirement based on a NOTE; no no-portable-oracle claim found to be over-suppression and no pending plan found vacuous. Source accounting only: no fixture, compiler invocation or execution credit.
